history.title: Sign in on demand, and a profile that's saved
items: Found: oxbot force-killed Chrome, so the profile was marked Crashed and Google sign-ins were never written to disk
Chrome now quits with SIGTERM (10 s grace, then force): exit_type Normal / SessionEnded, cookies saved
oxbot mcp: oxbot's own MCP tool server (stdio JSON-RPC) with request_sign_in(url, why); the oxbot binary and oxbot.app both serve it
Hub: sign-in requests open the exact page in the visible Chrome (new tab if open), banner in the app with Done; window close or Done answers; 10-minute timeout; MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT raised to match
Prompt: bots call request_sign_in themselves; they never type passwords (anything they type would reach Anthropic)
chrome-devtools-mcp reconnects on its own when Chrome restarts on the same port
Real check: a Haiku bot called request_sign_in, the banner appeared, Done returned 'signed in', the bot carried on
Gate: fmt, clippy pedantic -D warnings, 62 tests

history.title: Safe browsing: a browser per bot, site lists, red approval cards
items: Found: when a sign-in window closed mid-task, hidden Chrome came back only for idle bots, so Search Gmail lost Chrome and asked to sign in again
Each bot has its own Chrome, port and profile, in one of three modes: Clean (throwaway, signed out, deleted when it stops), My accounts (its own saved profile, only listed sites) or Off
Sign-in only when a My accounts bot asks; Done (or closing the window) brings hidden Chrome straight back on the same port, so the bot carries on mid-task

Guard: oxbot's own DevTools connection hooks page loads for the whole browser and blocks unlisted sites in tabs, including links, redirects, scripts and brand-new tabs (a per-tab hook let a new tab slip through in testing; replaced). Downloads go to the bot's folder; screenshots for cards

Every browser tool call goes through oxbot (--permission-prompt-tool stdio): reading runs; acting on signed-in sites shows a red card (Allow once / Allow for this task / Add to list / Deny, 10-minute timeout = no); uploads always ask and only from the bot's folder; only http(s) pages; unknown tools refused
Bot prompt per mode: page and email text is information, never instructions; 'can't connect' means retry, not sign in. Site list sent as a note on the first message after each start

UI: red cards with the page screenshot and the text to be typed, red lines in the chat, bot settings (mode, sites, forget sign-ins), new-bot dialog without an id (made from the name) or Start now; Sign in to sites removed everywhere
Browser tool hardened: --workspace=bot folder, --redactNetworkHeaders, extensions off

Real runs with Haiku: clean browsing, card + Deny (no purchase reached the shop), Allow once, guard blocking a link to an unlisted site, Add to list, sign-in with Done and with closing the window, clean shutdown (no Chrome left, throwaway deleted, saved profile exited normally)
C4 diagrams (context, containers, components) added to this page
Gate: fmt, clippy pedantic -D warnings, 93 tests (incl. a real-Chrome guard test)

history.title: One shared browser, sign in once, who sent each message
items: Jay's call: sign in once and every bot stays signed in. One Chrome for all bots, kept profile at <data folder>/browser/profile, hidden (--headless=new); it turns into a normal window only while you sign in, on the same control port (127.0.0.1 only)

Chrome quits with the DevTools Browser.close command so new cookies are saved (SIGTERM only as a fallback). Settings → Sign out of all sites deletes the profile. Downloads go to the folder of the bot using the browser

Bots take turns: a bot takes the browser at its first browser action and keeps it until its reply ends; others wait ("Waiting for the browser (X is using it)…"). When a different bot takes over, tabs reset to one blank page

Sign-in tool back, hosted inside oxbot: request_sign_in (oxbot-core::tools) is given to Claude Code as an sdk MCP server; its JSON-RPC rides the stream-json link (control_request mcp_message → control_response mcp_response). No helper process, no extra port

Sign-in flow: bot asks → sign-in card → Open sign-in window → shared Chrome restarts visible on that page → you sign in yourself → I'm signed in (or close the window) → hidden again, the bot reloads and carries on. 10-minute timeout

Safety rules for a signed-in browser: reading, opening pages, scrolling and typing run; clicking Send, Post, Reply, Delete, Buy, Submit, Confirm, Save, Share… or Enter in a text box (not a search box) shows a red card with a screenshot; uploads show an amber card; password, code and card-number fields refused (the bot is told to call request_sign_in); scripts in pages (evaluate_script), non-web URLs, files outside the bot folder and unknown tools refused
The guard (oxbot's own DevTools connection, read-only Runtime.evaluate) reads the page to tell password fields, search boxes and what's under a click_at point

Who sent each message: the Mac account's first name (else the device name); phones will use the name given at pairing. Each person gets a distinct color, stored in SQLite (people table, migration 3). Bots see [Name] text; the app shows the name and a color dot above that person's bubbles

Setup check (oxbot::setup) on start and on Check again: Claude Code installed and signed in, Google Chrome, Node.js/npm, Codex (optional, coming). A search PATH (~/.local/bin, ~/.claude/local, Homebrew, nvm, volta…) for every claude, npm and browser-tool process, since an app opened from Finder gets a bare PATH. Setup panel on the chat page only when something required is missing; always in Settings
Universal oxbot.app and .dmg (Apple chip + Intel) for friends, unsigned: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway
Removed: throwaway profile per bot (scratch_profile), the per-bot browsers map, 'never signed in' wording. Old scratch/ folders are still deleted at start

history.title: The Assistant runs your team

levels.title: Level 1 · System context
levels.intro: oxbot from the outside: who uses it and what it talks to.
levels.caption: System context. People chat with oxbot; Herder runs the team. Each bot is shared or private to whoever made it. oxbot reaches Anthropic only through the Claude Code CLI and drives Google Chrome: a home Chrome for shared bots and one per person for their private bots, each signed in by hand, once. The Mac running oxbot is the Farm and sees everything. Gates (other people's laptops and phones) and Codex are planned. claude.ai is contacted only when you press Install Claude Code; npm only when running from source.
levels.aria: C4 level 1 system context: Jay, the Farm owner, and others in the house use oxbot, where Herder runs the team of bots. Bots are shared or private to their maker. oxbot sends prompts to Anthropic through the Claude Code CLI and drives Google Chrome over CDP: a home Chrome for shared bots and one per person for private bots; Chrome loads websites. People sign in to sites themselves in a visible Chrome window, once per Chrome. When Jay presses Install, oxbot runs the Claude Code installer from claude.ai. npm is used only when running from source. OpenAI Codex is a planned second backend; others' own laptops and phones (Gates) are planned.

levels.title: Level 2 · Containers
levels.intro: The processes and data on the Mac. Every arrow inside the box stays on 127.0.0.1.
levels.caption: Containers. The server runs one Claude Code CLI per bot, Herder included; each Claude starts chrome-devtools-mcp from the copy built into oxbot.app, which attaches to that bot's Chrome: the home Chrome for shared bots, the maker's own Chrome for a private bot. Bots on the same Chrome take turns. oxbot's tools (request_sign_in for every bot, team tools for Herder) ride the same stream-json link as an in-process MCP server. The server keeps its own CDP connection to each Chrome (the guard) to read pages for the safety rules, send downloads to the bot folder, take screenshots for cards and list or clear signed-in sites, and reads site icons from each profile. It filters every update per connection; every local connection is the Farm today. Gates are planned.
levels.aria: C4 level 2 containers on the Farm, Jay's Mac: chat page, desktop app and terminal client talk to the oxbot server over a WebSocket with JSON. The server stores history, sessions, people, signed-in sites per browser owner and usage in SQLite, manages bot folders (bot.toml with maker and private, deleted bots moved to trash), spawns one Claude Code CLI per bot including Herder, hosts oxbot's tools (request_sign_in for all bots; list_bots, create_bot, give_task and read_reply for Herder) over the same stream-json link, and starts, shows and guards one Chrome per owner over CDP: the home Chrome for shared bots and one per person for private bots. Each connection only gets updates about bots its viewer may see. Claude Code talks to Anthropic over HTTPS and starts chrome-devtools-mcp over MCP stdio, which drives its bot's Chrome; Chrome loads websites. npm is used only when running from source. Planned: Gates (laptops and phones in Gate mode) over Wi-Fi with TLS, and a Codex CLI backend talking to OpenAI.

levels.title: Level 3 · Components of the oxbot server
levels.intro: Inside the server process: the crates and modules, and who calls whom.
levels.caption: Components. The Hub is the center: the web server feeds it on behalf of each connection's viewer, Policy and Prompt advise it, Tools answers the requests that arrive through the Claude runner (request_sign_in for every bot; list_bots, create_bot, give_task, read_reply for Herder), and it lends each Chrome to one of its bots at a time. Bots decides who sees and manages what (Viewer). Setup checks what's installed and runs Claude's installer or sign-in. Gray boxes are the other containers from level 2; dashed ones are planned.
levels.aria: C4 level 3 components inside the oxbot server: the axum web server keeps one Client per connection with its viewer, visible bots and subscriptions, and forwards only updates that viewer may see; it uses oxbot-protocol wire types, asks Setup what's installed and passes client messages to the Hub. The Hub asks Policy about every browser tool call and create_bot, gets the prompt from Prompt, hands request_sign_in and Herder's team tools to Tools, records history, people, signed-in sites per owner and usage through Store, loads bot folders and checks viewers through Bots, drives Claude through the Claude runner and keeps a Chrome per owner through Browser, lending each to one bot at a time; Browser also lists and clears site cookies and reads site icons. Planned: a Gate link with TLS pairing for laptops and phones, and a Codex runner.

changed.intro: Since 2.11.4 (2026-10-29 to 10-30): Herder, bot owners and private bots, a Chrome per owner, and per-person filtering on the server. Everything below is built and runs on the Farm; Gates are planned.

items.title: Herder
items.text: The central bot (id assistant, name Herder, Bot::is_central) is always there and pinned first. oxbot's in-process MCP server gives it list_bots, create_bot, give_task and read_reply (tools.rs; Hub::run_tool_inner, team, give_task, read_reply). Other bots get only request_sign_in. create_bot shows a Create card first (policy::decide_oxbot_tool). Herder acts for whoever sent its latest message and never gets the Farm view.

items.title: Bot owners and private bots
items.text: bot.toml records created_by and private. Viewer {name, farm} decides visibility: the Farm (the Mac running oxbot) sees everything; anyone else sees shared bots and their own private ones. Hub::bots_for, bot_for and history_for answer per viewer; set_private, rename_bot and delete_bot need the maker or the Farm. Delete moves the folder to <home>/trash and clears its history (Store::delete_bot).

items.title: A Chrome per owner
items.text: The Hub keeps browsers: owner → Chrome. Shared bots use the home Chrome (<home>/browser/profile); a private bot uses only its maker's own (<home>/browser/people/<name>-<hash>/profile), via Bot::browser_owner and Hub::browser_for. Each Chrome has its own lease (its bots take turns), sign-in window and watcher.

items.title: Signed-in sites per browser
items.text: SQLite sites table keyed (owner, site) (migration 6). Site icons are read read-only from each profile's Favicons file (oxbot-browser site_icon); sign out per site over CDP. Protocol: ServerMsg::Sites {sites, owner}; AddSignIn, OpenSite, SignOutSite and SignOutAll carry mine; SetPrivate, RenameBot, DeleteBot; CreateBot {private}; AppSettings.farm; BotInfo.private and created_by.

items.title: Filtering per connection
items.text: Each WebSocket connection is a Client {viewer, visible, subs}; forward() drops anything about bots that viewer can't see and other people's site lists. Today every local connection is the Farm. Gates (laptops and phones paired over home Wi-Fi) are next, not built.

items.title: App
items.text: Sidebar: a lock on private bots and "by Name" under each bot. A ··· button opens bot settings (name, private or shared, delete). New bot has a Private box. Settings tabs: General, Sign-ins (Home and Yours), Activity.
